# Samathabheda (Pvr 5)

**ID:** Pvr 5
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Samathabheda
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samathabheda* ("The legal issues and their settling") is the fifth text of the *Parivāra* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. In Hermann Oldenberg's edition of the Pali Vinaya, it is presented as the second main division of Chapter IV alongside the *Antarapeyyāla* (or *Anantarapeyyāla*) [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; Horner, Vinaya Pitaka 6]. However, early commentarial traditions enumerate sixteen *Parivāras*, treating *Anantarapeyyāla* and *Samathabheda* as two independent chapters, an arrangement reflected in the fact that each division possesses its own concluding summary verse (*uddāna*) [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka 6]. In English translation, the text has been rendered by I.B. Horner in *The Book of the Discipline* (Vol. VI) and by Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI].

The treatise details the circumstances under which each of the four classes of monastic legal procedures (*samatha*) is applied to settle ecclesiastical disputes (*adhikaraṇa*). I.B. Horner describes the section as functioning like an explanatory appendix to the preceding material, systematically resolving definitions of legal procedures that would otherwise encumber the exposition [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI]. Structurally, it begins with an analytical matrix (*mātikā*) formulated as a series of questions that are subsequently answered and expanded in detail, opening with a section designated as the *Pariyāyavāra* [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI].

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus corroborates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across these works, showing 697 matches with *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11) and 717 matches with the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), in addition to substantial shared material with later Vinaya literature such as the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi-ṭīkā*, *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*, and *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies automatic cross-language alignments with Sanskrit Vinaya texts (notably the *Adhikaraṇavastu* and *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*) and Tibetan canonical translations of the *Vinayavastu* and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus].
